title: sail configuration
description: sail's native configuration format (sing-box v1.14.2 JSON and sail's extensions)

ntp.description: sail ignores this field, with a warning: sail keeps the system's clock

certificate.description: The root certificates servers are checked against; the system's when unset.

certificate_providers.description: sail refuses this field: Certificates from ACME and other providers: the inbounds would serve none

http_clients.description: How sail fetches over HTTP, rule-sets for one, by tag.

network_namespaces.description: sail refuses this field: Linux network namespaces to listen and dial in

endpoints.description: Both an inbound and an outbound under one tag, as sing-box's endpoints: connections routed to the tag go out through it, and what comes in through it is routed with the tag as its inbound.

then.description: sail ignores this type, with a warning: sing-box's gRPC API, for its clients and dashboard to watch and control the instance

clash_api.description: The Clash API, which dashboards (yacd, metacubexd) and clients control the instance through. sing-box has it under `experimental`, which is read too, as the same.

outbound_providers.description: A sail extension: outbounds given together, downloaded, read from a file or written in place, that groups take as members, as Mihomo's proxy groups take a proxy-provider's proxies.

user_limits.description: A sail extension: what each user, by name, may do across every inbound it is in.

listen.description: Where the API listens; it is not served when unset.

certificate.description: Inline PEM, its lines one to an entry or all in one.

certificate_directory_path.description: Directories, every file of which holds certificates.

external_controller.description: Where it listens, `host:port`; an empty host is every address, as in Mihomo. Unset, it is not served, though `default_mode` still sets the mode rules match.

secret.description: What callers authenticate with, `Authorization: Bearer`, or a WebSocket's `?token=`. The API is served only with a strong one (at least 32 characters, 10 distinct): `sail generate secret` makes one.

external_ui.description: A directory of a dashboard's files, served at `/ui/`; relative to the data directory.

external_ui_download_url.description: Where the dashboard is downloaded from, a ZIP, when `external_ui` is empty. The core has none of its own: unset, nothing is downloaded, and a warning says so; a host, such as sail-cli, may give one.

external_ui_download_detour.description: The outbound the download goes through; the default one when unset.

access_control_allow_origin.description: The origins browsers may call it from (CORS); any when empty.

access_control_allow_private_network.description: Pages on public addresses may call it on a private one (Private Network Access).

default_mode.description: The mode rules match at the start, `Rule` when unset.

servers.description: The servers, each by its tag. None is the system's resolver alone.

rules.description: Which server a query goes to, matched in order.

final.description: The server of the queries no rule matches; the first one when unset.

reverse_mapping.description: Remembers the domain of each address the DNS answers that pass through carry, so that connections to the address are routed by the domain.

strategy.description: Which address families names resolve to, and in what order.

timeout.description: How long one query to one server may take; 10s when unset, as in sing-box.

disable_cache.description: No answer is kept: each query goes to its server.

disable_expire.description: Answers kept are used however old they are, until the cache is full or cleared.

cache_capacity.description: How many answers are kept; 1024 when unset, and at least that, as in sing-box.

optimistic.description: An answer that has expired is still given, for up to its timeout, while the server is asked again in the background.

client_subnet.description: The EDNS Client Subnet each query carries, unless a rule says otherwise.

independent_cache.description: sail ignores this field, with a warning: Each server's answers are kept apart, always: what this asks for

client_strategy.description: A sail extension: the address families the answers to clients' queries (hijack-dns, a DNS listener) carry, besides what `strategy` and the rules leave out: a family either leaves out is answered with no records. The instance's own lookups keep `strategy`. As Mihomo's `dns.ipv6: false` answers clients, while its connections still resolve IPv6.

timeout.description: How long after it expired an answer may still be given; 3d when unset, as in sing-box.

inbound.description: Tags of the inbounds the connection that needs the name came in through.

query_type.description: Record types, by name (`A`, `AAAA`, `HTTPS`) or number.

query_client_subnet.description: sail refuses this field: A condition sail does not match: the rule would match otherwise

query_dnssec.description: sail refuses this field: A condition sail does not match: the rule would match otherwise

auth_user.description: Names of the users an inbound authenticated.

clash_mode.description: The mode of Clash's API, as in a routing rule.

network_type.description: The kind of network: `wifi`, `cellular`, `ethernet`, `other`.

network_is_expensive.description: The network is metered, as the system says.

network_is_constrained.description: The network is in a low data mode, as the system says.

wifi_ssid.description: The network the host is on, as the routing rules match it.

wifi_bssid.description: The address of the Wi-Fi access point, `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`, in any case, with `:` or `-`, or as 12 hex digits.

default_interface_address.description: sail refuses this field: A condition sail does not match: the rule would match otherwise

source_mac_address.description: MAC addresses of the LAN device the query comes from, as the neighbor table and DHCP leases know it.

source_hostname.description: Host names of the LAN device the query comes from, as its DHCP lease has it.

rule_set.description: Tags of rule-sets, any of whose rules matching matches. Their `ip_cidr` rules match no query, which has no address yet.

response_answer.description: Records the response has among its answers, as `answer` writes them: any of them.

response_ns.description: Records the response has among its name servers.

response_extra.description: Records the response has among its additional records.

outbound.description: Tags of the outbounds that dial the name; of the rule itself, not of a rule a logical one combines.
